failures.rootCause: The agent read only the first ~35 lines of decomp.c, declared it understood the bitstream format, and then spent ~90 bash calls generating full-size encodings that produced empty decompressor output. It never isolated which stage broke, and the final deliverable was a Python traceback accidentally redirected into data.comp. The unrecoverable moment is the premature 'now I understand' claim on a partial read of the only spec that existed.
failures.firstUnrecoverableStep: Now I understand the decompressor. It's an arithmetic coding decompressor that expects: 1. An initial 9-bit integer indicating the number of items to decode

failures.rootCause: The agent wrote a literal placeholder sentence into the graded path data.comp and continued churning on encoder variants without ever replacing or re-checking the on-disk artifact. Budget expired with the stub still in place, so the deliverable was invalid regardless of encoder quality. Root cause is that the graded path was used as scratch space while the real work happened elsewhere.
failures.firstUnrecoverableStep: 1: This is a placeholder - the actual compressed data needs proper arithmetic coding implementation

failures.rootCause: The agent spent 73 turns on environment bootstrapping (pip installs, model download), then iterated per-row visual debugging by rendering crops/masks and Read-ing them back as images. Each image readback consumes large context and one full turn while advancing the algorithm marginally, so runway was exhausted mid-debug. The time sink is image-readback-based debugging where a numeric metric (IoU per row) would have localized the bug in one call.
